summary: Selenium sulphide is a topical antiseborrheic agent. OTC 1% shampoo helps control dandruff and seborrheic dermatitis by reducing flaking, itching, irritation, redness and scaling of the scalp; prescription strengths (2.25-2.5%) are used for tinea versicolor. It is applied to wet scalp/skin, left briefly, then rinsed thoroughly. For external use only - avoid the eyes. Systemic absorption is minimal with intact skin.
indications: Helps control dandruff (prevent recurrence of flaking and itching)
Helps control seborrheic dermatitis (itching, irritation, redness, flaking and scaling of the scalp)

moa: Selenium sulphide has cytostatic (antimitotic) activity on cells of the epidermis and follicular epithelium, reducing the rate of epidermal turnover and corneocyte production that drives the flaking of dandruff and seborrheic dermatitis. It also has antifungal activity against Malassezia (Pityrosporum) yeasts implicated in seborrheic dermatitis and tinea versicolor.

preg: Topical agent with minimal systemic absorption through intact skin; systemic risk is considered low. Not applicable for systemic dosing. Use during pregnancy only if needed and as directed; avoid prolonged use over large areas.
lact: Minimal systemic absorption from topical use; systemic exposure to a breastfed infant is expected to be negligible. Avoid application to the breast/chest area to prevent direct infant contact.
renal: Not applicable - topical agent with minimal systemic absorption; no dose adjustment.
hepatic: Not applicable - topical agent with minimal systemic absorption; no dose adjustment.

overdose: Topical overuse may cause increased local scalp/skin irritation, dryness, oiliness or hair loss - reduce frequency and use bland care. If accidentally swallowed, get medical help or contact a Poison Control Center (1-800-222-1222) right away; manage ingestion with supportive care.
